title: Lower bounds on entropy production from dynamical correlation functions
authors: Paul Raux, Alexander M. Maier, Udo Seifert
abstract: Entropy production is a key property in stochastic thermodynamics. For partially observed and coarse-grained systems, its inference is challenging and typically rests on proven lower bounds. We derive two versions of such bounds based on the asymmetry of experimentally accessible two-time correlation functions of coarse-grained state observables. For non-equilibrium steady states, the bound is valid for arbitrary correlation lag. For time-dependent processes, it requires the limit of vanishing lag. These bounds hold true for any system that follows either a Markovian dynamics or a coupled set of overdamped Langevin equations on some underlying, unobservable level of description. We illustrate the bounds for both types of dynamics and discuss their optimization and potential tightness.
summary: This paper establishes rigorous lower bounds on entropy production by analyzing the asymmetry of two-time correlation functions. It develops separate forms of these bounds for steady-state and time-dependent non-equilibrium processes. The results are highly relevant for characterizing irreversibility in complex physical systems using only experimentally accessible measurements.
main_problem: The primary goal is deriving rigorous lower bounds on entropy production (EPR) for systems where measurements are partial or coarse-grained.
main_result: Two key bounds are derived: one valid for Non-Equilibrium Steady States ($	ext{NESS}$) using arbitrary correlation lags, and another requiring the vanishing lag limit ($	au 	o 0$) for time-dependent processes.
method: The analysis relies on exploiting the asymmetry of experimentally accessible two-time correlation functions between state observables ($A$ and $B$), relating this asymmetry to path weights and KL divergence bounds derived from fluctuation theorems.
model_or_system: The theory applies to systems following Markovian dynamics or coupled overdamped Langevin equations. Examples include discrete-state Markov networks (e.g., four-state models) and continuous processes like particles on a ring potential.
key_observables: Entropy Production Rate ($	ext{EPR}$), two-time correlation function $C_{A,B}(t, 	au)$, and the correlation asymmetry $\chi_{A,B}(t, 	au)$.
important_parameters: Correlation lag ($	au$), time ($t$), system affinities, and potential amplitudes ($V_0$).
main_assumptions: The underlying dynamics must be Markovian on some microscopic level. For time-dependent processes, the bound derivation requires taking the limit of vanishing correlation lag ($	au 	o 0$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the performance and optimization of the derived bounds (e.g., showing Quality Factors $Q_{A,B}(	au)$ vs $	au$ or affinities) for both NESS and time-dependent driving scenarios.
paper_structure: The paper develops two main results: a bound applicable to steady states ($\hat{\sigma}_{A,B}(	au) \le \sigma$) and a second bound derived in the vanishing lag limit ($\hat{\sigma}_{A,B}(t) \le \sigma(t)$). It then applies these bounds to various physical models (Markov networks, Langevin dynamics) to test their tightness.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful theoretical tools for quantifying irreversibility and dissipation in complex systems using only measurable correlation functions, which is crucial for understanding open quantum systems where full state tomography is impossible.
